propositions: Ticket directories are created with os.makedirs OUTSIDE the write lock, and the first event file lands only after lock acquisition, leaving a vulnerable window where an interruption (kill, host sleep, timeout) strands an empty ticket directory that fsck reports as MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH.

Publishing dir and first CREATE event atomically via staging in .tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid4hex> directories and renaming under the write lock closes the interruption window; temp paths are invisible to fsck checks because they are dot-prefixed, matching existing exclusion rules.
Concurrent ticket creates do not collide on temp paths because staging names are suffixed with pid and uuid4; the existing write-lock discipline is unchanged.
Interrupted or failed batch operations roll back their staging trees and remove any ticket directories they created, preventing orphaned empty directories from accumulating.

Stale staging directories left by dead writer processes are removed via bounded best-effort sweep at writer start, using process-owner stamps to avoid pid recycling collisions, without touching actual ticket data or violating the 043f rule against writer-side cleanup of event-less ticket directories.
